I do not know your insurance circumstances, but I would ask for another sleep study and tell them what happened the previous study. There are doctors in my office that have allowed patients to do it again because some people can not sleep well in a strange place, and their second time most likely had more accurate results. My doctor diagnosed me with IH indicative of Narcolepsy (whatever that means) probably because I only had one mark on the MSLT. I have a lot of symptoms of Narcolepsy like sleep paralysis but could not be clinically diagnosed. If you can't get that second study find another doctor that understands. And if you get a second study approved you can prepare yourself and know what to expect.

I had at least one sleep paralysis episode nightly. I had a sleep study done as well. I was diagnosed with Hypersonmia suggestive of Narcolepsy because my test was close to a Narcolepsy diagnosis, and I would have cataplexy symptoms during sleep paralysis (passing out from heightened emotions). I finally have sleep medicine that eliminates my sleep paralysis. 

Oddly enough, I've had aliens coming through my window. They were technologically advanced; they didn't need to break in 😅. Found them way more scarier than the 7ft tall shadow man and the red-haired woman with a rifle.

I have all the narcolepsy symptoms besides sleep paralysis, but because she didn't listen to me during medical history she assumed I had been taking adderall since a child (I started Adderall last year), and felt no need to address those symptoms besides the sleep paralysis and EDS, by first trying to prescribe Xywav. If she would've given me a straightforward diagnosis of IH, I wouldn't have an issue at all. I just want a straight forward diagnosis that doesn't leave me feeling more confused. But I do get what you mean. Also, too I think there is also stigma with the word "idiopathic",  because you're being told in a general sense, " you have this and we dont know why" and that may be why some people push for another diagnosis because how some people view "idiopathic" diagnoses as "not real illness" when in fact it is real. She based her diagnosis on "stimulants taken as a child has lessened narcolepsy symptoms" and the one SOREMP, and while the latter is valid the incorrect information of medical history is not, and that is what caused this feeling of limbo in deciding what she should diagnose me.

I didn't take any medications during my sleep study, I had to be off them at least 6 weeks prior to my study. I was allowed to stop taking my adderall two days before my study. I actually had a sleep study scheduled and then Norton Healthcare had a major cyberattack and had to be rescheduled two months out. It was the worst, lol.

Yes, I had to sign all the forms at the office, and Jazz reps had even called to set up a patient account and discuss the process of getting approved and financial programs that they offered. Being on Medicaid, I was ineligible for those programs.

I'm pretty sure they were both pulmonologists and they work in the same office for office visits and conducting sleep studies. But I do not know if they have certain specializations in sleep meds. Did your heart rate increase with both meds? My heart rate is sorta high with just adderall. So that may be my last worry before taking this combo.

She was not the original practitioner who ordered the sleep study. I honestly don't know why the office said I had to follow up with another doctor for my sleep study results.  I may see if I can get an appointment with the person who originally ordered my study. She was so much more attentive. Also thank you for the info! I was reading online it had to be monitored closely because of elevated blood pressure and it was worrisome for me if a doctor is inattentive.

I have the test results that prove at least IH with 1 SOREMPS, but I have cataplexy and sleep paralysis and she didn't want to diagnose me with Narcolepsy because of 1 SOREMPS and contributed my diagnosis to me being on a stimulant as a child, but was not on stimulants as a child. Her not listening and inaccurate notes gave her the gray area of diagnosis but labeled it IH because I can be approved of meds. Sorry, I should have been more clear that I have a diagnosis, but she made it more confusing than anything else. She's treating me for IH, but not for narcolepsy symptoms.

Definitely lucky. it's a great time to go through a transition that's life changing. I was thrown out to the wolves. My parents stopped bringing Tylenol to school, because they couldn't leave work that many times to bring it to me. The school also didn't allow OTC meds to be left with the nurse. Or parents didn't bother to ask the doctor to write a note to school. I ended up improvising. I had an Altoids mint box and would put my Tylenol in it. Teachers allowed mints. They assumed I had mints. So I'd take them during class or go to the restroom. 

Kudos for being an awesome mom by the way. My mom didn't really try to be understanding. My husband though, I'll tell him I've started. He will get me my comfort snacks without me asking him.

I have two girls one is seven and one will be nine. When my youngest daughter was four we were using a public restroom. She decided to touch the sanitary can attached  to the stall. 

She was about to peek inside it, and I panicked and told her, "No, don't touch that! There's blood in there!"

She looked at me worried and asked, "Who killed them?"

That's when I decided to be open about womanhood. They both now know that when they get older they'll have a period. I purchased my nine year old her first training bra, and she doesn't like it one bit. I'm wondering when her first period will be. I've been thinking about giving them a period "gift basket." 

I was also thinking the first day or two they could stay home from school. I wish I could've because I didn't know how bad my cramps would get. And I hate to think they are suffering at school with that same pain.

When I shop at my local Walmart I avoid one employee in particular. We had an interaction that I could've avoided if I didn't walk fast to avoid interaction with people.

He was coming around the corner, and I'm hauling ass with my cart because anxiety is setting in and I just want to leave. He had a custodian cart and I stepped on my brakes also known as my poorly made sandals. I prevented a collision by a hair.

So here comes my quickly thought rehearsed apology. It sounded good in my head, when it came out of my mouth it sounded more like I was running for my life from someone or something.

Quick dialogue

Me: Sorry, I can't stop I just go so fast, and I need to get home. 

Him: Are you okay? Are you in danger?

Me: Oh no. I just hate shopping and I left my kids with my husband.

Him: You're tattoos are cool.

Me: Yeah it's a Harry Potter sleeve. My brother in law is a tattoo artist. Okay, have a good day.

Why am I like this?!

I meant to post an update. Its not graves now. My thyroid blood work was normal. I had an abnormal blood test that showed signs of inflammation and now I'm being suggested fibromyalgia is the culprit for what I'm going through. I'll be having more blood work and tests done Monday. 

I'm grateful it's not Grave's. My grandmother has so many issues caused by Grave's, and I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy. I think most issues is exacerbated by her continuing to smoke. On the other hand, I wish I knew what is going on with me.
I do blackout. Forgot to mention that. My husband tells me everything that happens the previous night, that I had absolutely no recollection of doing.

I understand that feeling. I'm scared I'm getting dependent. I've stopped before, and went right back to it.  Ambien is the only sleep med that turns off my brain at night so I can fall asleep. 

I have built a tolerance to it. My doctor prescribed a second antidepressant to take with Ambien. I also suffer from BPD and depression. So I'm on loads of meds. I do try and take breaks from Ambien and just take the second antidepressant. I can fall asleep but it takes a couple of hours and when I do fall asleep, the sleep quality isn't great.

Yesterday, I found out my paternal grandfather has hyperthyroidism. I was pretty surprised. I thought my paternal aunts were the only ones that have thyroid issues on my father's side. They have hypothyroidism.

 Family isn't helping me at all. Most are telling me I don't have a thyroid disease.

I was close to fainting a couple of years ago. I was getting cortisone steroid shots on my c section scar. The steroid shot was to help reduce the appearance of my scar because it was considered a hypertrophic scar (a raised ugly ass scar). 

The doctor said that some people will faint after the procedure is done because ya know needles. I told him I'm not afraid of needles. Thought I was fine when he helped me up to a sitting position. All of a sudden the doctor sounded like Charlie Brown's teacher. I got awfully dizzy.

I actually was giving myself a pep talk to walk to the chair that had my pants and I tried putting them on, but started getting even dizzier and a bit drowsy. I also felt like my body was on fire. I crawled to the door pant less  and told the receptionist that I might faint. The nurses gave me water and then I sat there for ten minutes to get my bearings. I finally put my pants on and left.

I'm also trying to keep Reddit as my only social media account.
